Regionshospitalet Gødstrup is a regional healthcare facility in Denmark that participates in the national DANIBD database for inflammatory bowel disease (IBD) treatment and quality assurance. In the 2024 DANIBD annual report, the hospital provided detailed operational analyses and formal consultation responses regarding specific quality indicators [^src1]. 

One of the hospital's key contributions to the national quality discussion involves its audit of [[indikator-6|Indikator 6]], which tracks re-operation rates [^src1]. Regionshospitalet Gødstrup reviewed seven patient courses involving re-operations, all of which were performed due to suspected surgical complications [^src1]. The audit revealed that surgical complications were confirmed in three cases, while no signs of surgical complications were found in the remaining four [^src1]. Based on this review, the hospital concluded that the re-operation rate is a poor quality metric for IBD treatment, as a patient might be in poor condition post-surgery due to the surgical stress response rather than a true surgical complication [^src1]. Instead, the hospital argues that [[anastomoselaekage|anastomoselækage]] is a much more relevant and accurate measure of surgical quality, noting that re-operation rates are not used as quality metrics in cancer surgery either [^src1].

In terms of diagnostic performance, Regionshospitalet Gødstrup was identified as one of four departments—alongside [[hvidovre|Hvidovre]], [[ouh-svendborg|OUH Svendborg]], and [[aarhus-universitetshospital|Aarhus Universitetshospital]]—that failed to meet the target for [[indikator-1a|Indikator 1a]] [^src2]. Specifically, less than 70% of newly diagnosed adult patients at these facilities were investigated in accordance with the recommended guidelines [^src2]. This highlights an area for operational improvement within the broader national effort to standardize IBD diagnostics.
